-- The untrusted plugin. It receives a confined `fs` and reads what it asks for.
plugin(path: str) -> str uses fs =
  pre path.char_count() > 0
  post out.char_count() >= 1
  let mine = fs.read(path) else ""
  let theirs = fs.read("notes/../secret.txt") else ""
  mine + "|" + theirs

-- Runs the plugin with `fs` narrowed to `notes`, so `path` is relative to `notes`.
-- Anything the plugin reads outside `notes` yields "".
-- The result always contains the "|" separator, so it is never empty.
run_plugin(path: str) -> str uses fs =
  pre path.char_count() > 0
  post out.char_count() >= 1
  -- Assumes notes/nofile.txt and notes/secret.txt do not exist, so both reads give "".
  ex run_plugin("nofile.txt") == "|"
  with fs = fs.sub("notes")
    return plugin(path)
